output.subject: We've received your complaint about your debit card being declined in Nashville
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for getting in touch with us. We have received your complaint, and we want you to know that a person has read it carefully.

You told us that while you were in Nashville for a work conference, your debit card was declined at a restaurant and then again at the hotel front desk. You mentioned that you received a text asking whether you had made the purchase, that you replied YES twice, and that the card still kept being declined. You also told us that your brother-in-law had to cover dinner for the whole table.

You said you understand why fraud protection exists, but you want to know what the point of the text is if answering it doesn't change anything. You have asked us to fix the problem, and you told us you are prepared to close all of your accounts with us if it isn't resolved.

We're sorry for the frustration and inconvenience this has caused, especially while you were away for work.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Check whether the card is still being declined. If the customer may still be travelling, a faster phone call may be needed in addition to this letter.
Confirm the actual reason for each decline and how the customer's YES replies to the texts were received and handled.
The customer has threatened to close all their accounts. Consider whether a relationship or retention contact is appropriate.
The customer has not asked to be reimbursed for the dinner. Decide whether anything should be said about it.
This reply takes no position on the substance and does not name the reviewing team, as required in acknowledge-only mode.
